---
title: "A collapsed Gibbs sampler for the CRP mixture"
subtitle: "Catalog P-13 · rung 8 · after Broderick (MLSS 2016, part III)"
description: "Posterior inference one point at a time: each point's new cluster is chosen with probability proportional to the CRP prior weight times the fit."
toc: false
---

The last rung runs the model backwards: given the data, which clusters? The collapsed Gibbs
sampler (Neal's Algorithm 3) visits one point at a time. It takes the point out of its
cluster and puts it back with probability proportional to

- n_c × (fit of the point to cluster c), for each existing cluster c, or
- alpha × (fit of the point to a brand-new cluster),

where n_c is the number of other points in cluster c. The first factor is the Chinese
restaurant prior; the second is the likelihood with the cluster centre integrated out.

## What to try

- **Step point** (or Enter) a few times and compare the two bars: the CRP prior weight
  says "join a big cluster"; the posterior multiplies in how well the point fits each
  cluster. The dashed piece is a new cluster.
- **Start from one cluster, singletons or a random split.** From one cluster the sampler
  splits off the four true clusters within a sweep or two; from 100 singletons or a random
  split it merges them over ten to twenty sweeps, because single points move one at a time.
- **alpha.** The demo in Broderick's tutorial fixes alpha = 0.01, so a new cluster starts
  with one hundredth of the weight of a one-point cluster. That is a strong prior. Move
  alpha to 1 or 10 while playing: the sampler keeps more small clusters, and the level
  of K in the trace moves up.
- **true means** overlays the four centres the data came from.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The number of clusters here, K after a sweep, is a draw from the posterior of K_J for
J = 100 units, not a prior statement. The sampler holds sigma = 1 and a N(0, 3²) prior on
cluster centres fixed. After Broderick (MLSS 2016, part III, demo 7); the sampler is
re-implemented in the site's engine (`gibbs.ts`) and no code is copied.
:::

Standalone version: [embed/crp-gibbs.html](../../embed/crp-gibbs.html), for example
`?preset=singletons`, `?alpha=1&n=20`.
